qs.q: A patient presents with paralysis of the right vocal cord, right-sided Horner syndrome, and ipsilateral shoulder drop. Where is the anatomical lesion most likely located?
o: Injury to the vagus nerve trunk within the carotid sheath.
Involvement of the recurrent laryngeal nerve in the thoracic cavity.
Damage to the superior laryngeal nerve near the thyroid gland.
Lesion at the skull base affecting multiple cranial nerves.
Pathology at the cerebellopontine angle involving the facial nerve.
qs.e: Collet-Sicard syndrome involves lesions at the skull base affecting cranial nerves IX, X, XI, and XII.
qs.s: Weekly Year 5: ENT Exam - November 6, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: A 60-year-old man with a 40 pack-year smoking history presents with right shoulder pain, Horner syndrome, and weakness of the right hand. A computed tomography scan reveals a mass at the superior sulcus of the right lung. Which anatomic structure's involvement explains the Horner syndrome?
o: D. Phrenic nerve descending along pericardium
B. Lower trunk of the brachial plexus network
C. Recurrent laryngeal nerve within thorax
A. Cervical sympathetic chain and ganglion
E. Vagus nerve trunk within superior mediastinum
qs.e: Pancoast tumors in the superior sulcus can compress the cervical sympathetic chain, resulting in classic ipsilateral Horner syndrome.
qs.s: Weekly Pathology Exam - November 6, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: An adult male suffers a stab wound to the right side of his neck, resulting in Horner's syndrome on that side. Disruption of which sympathetic pathway causes this?
qs.e: Horner's syndrome results from interruption of the cervical sympathetic chain supplying the head.
qs.s: Weekly Year 1: Anatomy Exam - October 30, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: A patient with an apical lung mass, Horner syndrome, and ulnar nerve pain. What is the diagnosis?
o: Pancoast (superior sulcus) tumour at the lung apex.
Superior vena cava obstruction causing facial swelling.
qs.e: Pancoast tumors occur at the lung apex and invade the sympathetic chain (Horner syndrome) and the brachial plexus (C8-T2 distribution pain).
qs.s: Weekly Pathology Exam - March 7, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)
